recommendations.issue: Goodwill and reader focus scores 0 of 4. Rewrite sentences that start with the author so they start with the reader and what they get.
recommendations.original: We offer a comprehensive onboarding programme.
recommendations.rewrite: You will be up and running in your first week, with a guide on call.

recommendations.issue: Borrowed credibility scores 0 of 4. Replace vague praise with a named source, their role and the outcome they got.
recommendations.rewrite: "We cut month-end close from 9 days to 3." Priya Shah, Finance Director, Northwind Logistics

recommendations.issue: Competence and judgement scores 1 of 4. Replace what you were responsible for with what changed because of you: action verb, what you did, measurable result.
recommendations.original: Responsible for managing the engineering team.
recommendations.rewrite: Grew the engineering team from 6 to 25 and cut release time from monthly to daily.

recommendations.issue: Stakes: pain and desire scores 0 of 4. Describe the specific moment the reader realises the current way is not working, in their words.
recommendations.rewrite: It is 11pm on the last day of the quarter and you are still matching receipts to bank lines.

recommendations.issue: Story and narrative scores 0 of 4. Insert a three-sentence story: who, what went wrong, what changed. Put it where the claim needs most belief.
recommendations.rewrite: Sam ran a gym losing 30 members a month. We changed one thing: a call on day 7. Churn halved by spring.

recommendations.issue: Identity, status and belonging scores 1 of 4. Connect acting with who the reader is or aspires to be.
recommendations.rewrite: Join 4,000 engineering leaders who get one practical idea every Tuesday.

recommendations.issue: Objection handling scores 0 of 4. Name the sceptic's strongest objection and answer it with evidence. Two-sided beats one-sided for sceptical readers.
recommendations.rewrite: Yes, we cost more than a freelancer. You are paying for a team that does not disappear in August.

recommendations.issue: Mechanism and reasoning scores 1 of 4. After each claim, add 'because...' or 'which means...'.
recommendations.rewrite: Our coffee tastes better because we roast to order and ship within 48 hours.

recommendations.issue: Structure and flow scores 2 of 4. Put the main claim or outcome in the first line. Build the case after.
recommendations.original: Founded in 2010, we have worked across many sectors... (point in paragraph 4)
recommendations.rewrite: We cut onboarding time in half for B2B SaaS teams. Here is how.

recommendations.issue: Cost of delay scores 0 of 4. Show what staying put costs per week, month or year, using the reader's numbers where possible.
recommendations.original: Don't wait to fix your hiring process.
recommendations.rewrite: Each month a senior role stays open costs roughly [£X] in delayed delivery.

recommendations.issue: The call to act scores 0 of 4. End with a single, specific, low-friction action and say what happens when the reader takes it.
recommendations.original: Let us know if you have any questions.
recommendations.rewrite: Reply 'yes' and I will send two times for a 20-minute call next week.

recommendations.issue: Fit to the moment scores 1 of 4. Connect the message to a current shift, event or season the reader recognises.
recommendations.rewrite: Since your competitors started shipping AI features this year, buyers now expect them in every demo.

recommendations.issue: Telos scores 1 of 4. Write the single sentence you want the reader to remember. Put it near the start, repeat it at the end, and cut anything that doesn't serve it.
recommendations.original: (Five equal points about features, pricing, history, team and roadmap)
recommendations.rewrite: One idea: we halve your onboarding time. Everything else is evidence for that.

recommendations.issue: Mythos scores 0 of 4. Frame the message inside a bigger narrative: an old world, a shift, winners and losers, a promised land.
recommendations.rewrite: Buyers now do 70% of their research before talking to sales. The teams winning have stopped pitching and started teaching.

recommendations.issue: Length scores 0 of 4. Cut anything that doesn't serve the one big idea; aim for the usual range for this content type.
recommendations.rewrite: (The same email at 120 words, with one ask)

recommendations.issue: Structure scores 1 of 4. Put the main point or ask in the first two sentences, then order the rest as reasons, proof, next step.
recommendations.original: We have been operating since 2010 and offer many services... (ask in the final paragraph)
recommendations.rewrite: We can halve your onboarding time. Here's how, and what it would take.

recommendations.issue: Cohesion scores 1 of 4. Link ideas explicitly with connectives, repeat key terms instead of synonyms, and start paragraphs by picking up the last thread.
recommendations.original: Costs rose. Our team is experienced. Clients like us.
recommendations.rewrite: Costs rose, so clients need a partner who can deliver for less. That's where our experience helps.

recommendations.issue: Fit to this reader scores 2 of 4. Write to the reader's level and lead with what they care about; cut background they already know.
recommendations.original: (A technical deep-dive sent to a board member)
recommendations.rewrite: (One page on cost, risk and the decision needed)

recommendations.issue: Brief or detailed scores 1 of 4. Brief: headline and essentials; detail on request. Detailed: process, specifics, guarantees and risk mitigation up front.
Restrained or expressive scores 1 of 4. Restrained: understated, factual, calm. Expressive: warmth, enthusiasm and personal feeling are welcome.

Supplier on-time delivery was 91.3%. Headcount closed at 412, with 23 leavers and 31 joiners. The warehouse management system upgrade is 60% complete. Customer satisfaction scored 7.9 out of 10.
